gaps.why_now: The shared Phase 12 build gate now includes a dedicated libbpf survey checkpoint so this heavy helper consumer stays reviewable beside the existing virtio and storage lanes.
The existing make target keeps the Phase 12 survey tranche runnable through the same bounded entry point the other complex-driver lanes already use.
The earlier segment catalog already breaks libbpf into helper-first and high-risk clusters, which is exactly the roadmap discipline Phase 12 requires before any larger libbpf surface widens.
The landed enum-to-name tables provide a proven low-risk libbpf foothold with stable output semantics and no dependency on object loading, verifier interactions, or syscalls.

The landed CPU mask helper now covers bounded string parsing, set-bit counting, and a deferred chunk-reader interface for sysfs-style buffered input that future perf-buffer and feature-probe work can share without widening into direct file I/O or runtime loader behavior.

The landed perf-buffer poll helper keeps wait-result normalization, ready-buffer bookkeeping, and per-buffer slot access reviewable without widening into epoll wiring, mmap-backed ring ownership, online-CPU routing, or callback delivery.
A dedicated survey gate keeps the roadmap placement explicit now that libbpf helper work started earlier under the tooling tranche but the heavy-consumer rollout still belongs to Phase 12.

The shared Phase 12 build packet already replays the focused zigux_segments verify surface, so the manifest should count that compile-and-entrypoint gate explicitly instead of hiding it behind the broader survey and reviewability tests.

The Phase 12 lane should verify that the landed zigux_segments foundations still compile, that the dedicated zigux_segments verify surface stays wired into the same build packet, and that the manifest matches which segment files are landed versus still deferred, instead of relying only on older Phase 8 coverage.

The shared Phase 12 reviewability packet now exact-checks the ordered five-helper snapshot digest through a dedicated replay, so the manifest should keep that deterministic proof explicit instead of leaving it folded into the broader reviewability gate.
The lane needs a current note that explains how the existing helper slices fit into the Phase 12 heavy-helper consumer plan instead of leaving libbpf stranded in older Phase 8 wording.

The landed logging helper keeps libbpf print-level parsing, version reporting, and errno-string glue table-driven and output-stable without widening into environment reads, stderr output, or syscall-backed behavior.
The landed pin-path helper keeps bpffs path joining and dot-sanitization reviewable through bounded buffer APIs before any mkdir, statfs, unlink, or object-loader work enters the lane.

The landed helper-only fdinfo map-info parser and proc-fd path builders keep the shared bridge packet reviewable without widening into direct procfs reads, pinned-object reopen attempts, or descriptor ownership side effects.
The landed reused-map name resolution and compatibility summary keep the nearer libbpf bridge checks explicit without widening into close-on-replacement, token opens, or full pinned-map reopen flow.

The heavier shared file-path and handle bridge still crosses real procfs reads, bpffs opens, token creation, `bpf_obj_get()` reopen flow, and fd ownership semantics, so Phase 12 should keep it explicit as its own deferred bridge bucket instead of folding it into the later object-model blockers.

The online-CPU routing path still combines sysfs reads, `perf_event_open` setup, mmap-backed ring state, map updates, epoll registration, and timeout-sensitive polling, so it stays a separate deferred queueing-risk bucket beside the bounded helper surfaces that feed it.

The shared segment catalog already isolates skeleton population as the nearest post-helper libbpf cluster, but it still depends on `bpf_object`, `bpf_map`, and `bpf_program` model parity that the repo has not started yet.

ELF collection, object-loader setup, relocation recording, and load-time verifier interactions remain a broader follow-on risk even after the nearer helper-only bridge foundations and the later skeleton boundary, so the roadmap keeps this heavier slice deferred as its own reviewable loader bucket.

BTF fixups, extern resolution, relocation recording, and load-time verifier interactions remain a distinct verifier-facing cluster after the nearer helper-only bridge and object-model blockers, so the Phase 12 manifest should keep that deferred surface explicit instead of implying object-loader work is the final blocked libbpf segment.
